components.basis: Partial sums, centering, zero rate with positive denominators, log n from n = 2, finite modification convention.
Durrett Lemma 2.2.13 (pp. 63-64) for extended W and all p > 0 with Tonelli proof, integer-tail bounds, both decreasing-sum bounds, the m^{1/p-1} sum bound and the shift inequality, all proved.

components.gap: Supply, on the handbook route, the source's complete treatment of Durrett's Theorem 2.5.11 (Version 5, 11 January 2019, p. 87): (i) the conclusion of the Remark that, by comparison with the law of the iterated logarithm limsup S_n/(n^{1/2}(log log n)^{1/2}) = sigma*sqrt(2) a.s. (Theorem 8.5.2), the rate of Theorem 2.5.11 'is not far from the best possible' -- the routed text reproduces the LIL display (body 303-312) but omits this conclusion and states only that no optimality is asserted (body 79-81, 310-312); (ii) the Section 2.5.1 opening claim that one of the advantages of the random-series proof of the strong law is that it provides estimates on the rate of convergence of S_n/n -> mu. components.basis: Statement and proof of Theorem 2.5.11 are complete (a_n choice, variance series, Theorems 2.5.6/2.5.9 analogues, sigma = 0 and mean-mu variants). Source p. 87 opened: the Remark ends "so the last result is not far from the best possible" and Section 2.5.1 opens with the advantages claim; neither is on the route.
Power cutoff Y_m = X_m 1(|X_m| <= m^{1/p}) as in Durrett p. 87, boundary convention and contrast with the strict Feller cutoff.

Theorem 2.5.12 (pp. 87-88) with the Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund attribution and the E X^2 = infinity situation; annex gives the source interval decomposition, the (p/(2-p))(n-1)^{(p-2)/p} comparison, an explicit constant, the mean estimate and the C n^{1/p} sum.
Declared extension 0 < p < 1 with full proof.
Exercise 2.5.2 (p. 90) converse for every p > 0 with centering c, proved; centering forced for p >= 1.
Both regimes 0 < p < 1 and 1 <= p < 2 with necessity and sufficiency proved; endpoint p = 2 excluded with its counterexample.
Positive a_n with a_n/n nondecreasing (Durrett "a_n/n increasing", p. 89), W, q_n, Q, strict truncation Y_n = X_n 1(|X_n| < a_n), a_0 = 0 interval convention.

components.basis: Statement and both branches of the proof of Theorem 2.5.13 (pp. 89-90) are complete on the route, including identity (*), the variance and mean arguments and a_n/n -> infinity. Source p. 88 opened: the Section 2.5.2 opening (St. Petersburg a.s. behaviour, Feller (1946), no nonzero a.s. limit, Theorem 2.3.8 as a_n = n) is absent from the route.
Four computed examples (fair signs, dyadic square-root law, (7/4)x^{-11/4} density, dyadic law with a_n = n and n^2), all moments and threshold sums computed.

Explicit staircase a_n with existence of every N_k, convergent threshold series and infinite limsup proved.
